If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and forecast peaks >+3% above recent high, cap forecast at +2% deviation for mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and true outcome dips below 2% below forecast, apply 1.0–1.5% downward correction for late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect fading momentum.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day for early horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If forecast consistently overestimates by >1.5% for 3 consecutive days, apply 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment for mid horizon to correct for model bias.  
If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) and forecast remains above 75.0, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for late horizon to reflect weak market sentiment.
